course.title: CISSP Capstone: Six Releases
course.audience: Build a whole security program across all eight domains, release by release, to federal-ready.
course.description: Build a security program for a company moving to the cloud. Eight domain sheets, six releases: documented, specified, proven, tested and federal-ready, each raising the maturity score.

roles.name: Architecture & Network (Security Architect)

roles.name: Identity & Operations (Operations Lead)
roles.mission: Identity, access, logging, incident response and recovery.

steps.title: Open the evidence ledger
steps.description: A Git repository is the dated record.
steps.instruction: Create the ledger repository and make its first, empty commit.
instructionList: Open a terminal in your home folder.
Run the command; the folder name is ridgeline-program.
Every sheet, scan and transcript is hashed into ledger.sha256 here from now on.

commands.cmd: git init ridgeline-program && cd ridgeline-program && git commit --allow-empty -m "ledger opened"
commands.explain: Creates the repository the ledger lives in and makes a first commit with no files, so the ledger has a dated start.

flags.meaning: create an empty repository in a new folder
commit even though nothing is staged

commands.sample:
Initialized empty Git repository in /home/student/ridgeline-program/.git/
[main (root-commit) a1b2c3d] ledger opened

Initialized empty Git repository in /home/student/ridgeline-program/.git/
[main (root-commit) a1b2c3d] ledger opened

steps.title: Write the security policy (D1 v1)
steps.instruction: Write ten shall statements, five owned risks, and the AI uses with owners.
instructionList: Statement: “Access to systems holding customer data shall require multi-factor authentication.” — ten like it, no product names.
Rank the five security concepts for the product; give one example each of due care and due diligence.
Risk rows: “No approved policy (S-1) · Governance · write and approve” and four more, each with an owner.
The four AI uses, each with an owner; this replaces the 2019 “IT rules” — S-1 closed.
steps.expectedOutput: D1 shows ten testable shall statements, an approver and owner, five owned risks, the four AI uses with owners, and no product name.

docs.title: NIST CSF 2.0 — Govern
docs.lookFor: GV.PO (policy), GV.RR (roles), GV.SC (supply chain): the categories D1 fills

docs.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 — Annex A themes
docs.lookFor: the four themes (organizational, people, physical, technological) your handling rules map to

fixes.symptom: A statement names a product (“Keycloak shall…”)
fixes.fix: Products go in standards. Rewrite as the outcome: “administrative access shall require a second factor”.

fixes.symptom: Two risks share one owner for everything
fixes.fix: Owners are the role that can change the thing; spread them across the three roles honestly.

steps.whatItMeans: The policy is the top of the hierarchy every standard hangs from. No product names belong in it, so it survives the tools changing.

steps.title: Inventory the assets (D2 v1)
steps.instruction: Grow the inventory to fifteen owned assets and define four classification levels.
instructionList: Row: “Service Hub database · Architecture · Restricted · cloud account”; fifteen rows, one owner each.
Levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted — one handling rule each, e.g. “Restricted: encrypted at rest, access logged”.
Customer data locations: every row that holds it says so in the location column.
steps.expectedOutput: D2 lists fifteen assets with exactly one owner and a classification each, and four levels with one handling rule each.

docs.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 — Annex A themes
docs.lookFor: the four themes (organizational, people, physical, technological) your handling rules map to

docs.title: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 — media sanitization
docs.lookFor: the clear / purge / destroy table by media type; the record you keep

fixes.symptom: An asset has two natural owners
fixes.fix: Pick the one who would be called when it breaks; note the other as custodian in week 2.

fixes.symptom: Fewer than fifteen assets come to mind
fixes.fix: Count the phones, the sensors, the identity provider, the backups, the file share and the Git repository.

steps.whatItMeans: An asset with two owners has none in practice. The inventory is what every later control, scan and migration is measured against.

steps.title: Score the program and sign v1 (D6)
steps.description: The first number; the release note.
steps.where: ridgeline-program · terminal, then D6 and the Release Note
steps.instruction: Hash the eight sheets, write the Current Profile, score each domain, sign v1.
instructionList: Export each sheet as 0N_….md into the repository, then run the command.
D6 Profiles: a row per CSF function with its current state; score: eight domains at 1 = 8 of 32.
Three largest gaps into the remediation plan with owners and dates.
Release Note v1: shipped “eight sheets documented”; score 8; open “S-2 to S-10”; CEO signs.

commands.explain: Hashes the eight sheet files into the ledger and counts the lines, one per sheet, so the release has a verifiable manifest.

docs.title: NIST CSF 2.0 — Profiles
docs.lookFor: the Current and Target Profile templates; one row per category, score it 0–4

docs.title: coreutils — sha256sum
docs.lookFor: the -c option: check every hash in a list and print OK or FAILED per file

fixes.symptom: The count is less than 8
fixes.fix: A sheet is not exported yet or is misnamed. ls 0*_*.md and fix the prefix (01_ to 08_).

fixes.symptom: The CEO asks why the score is so low
fixes.fix: Level 1 means “written down with an owner”. That is the honest start; v2 adds numbers and reaches 16.

steps.whatItMeans: The score is the one number the CEO and the customer both read. Starting at 8 of 32 is honest, and every release is measured against it.

tasks.title: Write architecture and network
tasks.objective: Write D3 and D4 at v1: the architecture with trust boundaries, shared responsibility, and the network zones.

D4 has zones, ten or fewer allowed flows, and a default-deny statement

handoff.note: Scored in D6.

steps.title: Draw the architecture (D3 v1)
steps.instruction: Draw the boundaries and write five rows of shared responsibility.
instructionList: Boundaries: office, cloud account, suppliers (model provider, customer IdP); a line where each meets.
Shared row: “Physical data-centre security · Cloud provider”; “Gateway configuration · Company”; “Model training data · Model provider”; two more.
State encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest (provider-managed keys), and what the office protects physically.
steps.expectedOutput: D3 holds the boundary diagram, five shared-responsibility rows each with one owner, and the encryption and physical statements.

docs.title: draw.io — diagrams as files
docs.lookFor: saving as .drawio in the repository so the diagram is versioned with the sheets

docs.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — control catalogue
docs.lookFor: the control text for each id in your statements (PM-1, SC-7, IA-2…); copy its wording

fixes.symptom: A control seems owned by both sides
fixes.fix: Split it: the provider owns the service, the company owns its configuration. Two rows, two owners.

fixes.symptom: You cannot say where keys are held
fixes.fix: Write “provider-managed, to be confirmed” and add it to week 2’s cryptography standard.

steps.whatItMeans: Shared responsibility is where most cloud breaches start: a control each side assumed the other owned. Five rows make the seam visible.

steps.title: Draw the network zones (D4 v1)
steps.instruction: Define the zones, list at most ten allowed flows, and state default deny.
instructionList: Zones: office, cloud management, Service Hub, technicians, sensors.
Flow row: “Office → Cloud management · 443/tcp”; “Technicians → Service Hub · 443/tcp”; ten rows or fewer.
Default deny: “All flows are denied except those listed.” Remote administration path: VPN then 443 — nothing direct.
steps.expectedOutput: D4 shows the zones, ten or fewer allowed flows with port and protocol, the default-deny statement, and the remote administration path.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-207 — zero trust
docs.lookFor: the tenets; “default deny, every flow explicit” is tenet 2 and 3

docs.title: nftables — quick reference
docs.lookFor: a chain with policy drop and an accept rule: default deny with allowed flows

fixes.symptom: You need more than ten flows
fixes.fix: Group by zone pair and port; “office → hub 443” covers every office machine. More than ten means the zones are too fine.

fixes.symptom: The sensors need an inbound flow
fixes.fix: They do not; they send outbound only. A flow to a sensor is a finding, not a rule.

steps.whatItMeans: S-4 is that everything can reach everything. Default deny with a short allowed-flows list is the rule that closes it in week 3.

steps.title: Write the access rules (D5 v1)
steps.instruction: Map six roles against systems and write the MFA and account rules.
instructionList: Access rows: “Dispatcher · Service Hub · Write”; “Auditor · Logs · Read”; six roles across the systems.
MFA rule: “MFA for all administrative access; no shared accounts.” It closes S-2 and S-3 in week 3.
Joiner and leaver: “access granted on day one by the manager’s ticket; removed within one business day of leaving”.
steps.expectedOutput: D5 shows six roles against systems, the MFA and no-shared-accounts rule, and joiner and leaver steps with time limits.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-63-4 — digital identity
docs.lookFor: the authenticator assurance levels; AAL2 is what MFA on admin access means

docs.title: NIST SP 800-63B — authenticators
docs.lookFor: the multi-factor authenticator types; which ones count as a second factor

fixes.symptom: A role needs admin on everything
fixes.fix: That is a separation-of-duties problem for week 2. For v1 record it as written, and flag it as a risk.

fixes.symptom: “One business day” feels slow
fixes.fix: Then write the number you can meet: “within 4 hours” is a promise you will be tested on in week 5.

steps.whatItMeans: S-2 and S-3 are a shared admin login and optional MFA. The rule written here is what you prove in the lab in week 3.

steps.title: Write operations (D7 v1)
steps.instruction: State what is logged and for how long, the incident first hour, and backups.
instructionList: Logging: “authentication, administrative actions, Hub requests — kept 90 days” (v2 raises this).
Incident first hour: confirm, contain, notify the Head of Security; the customer notice clock is 72 hours.
Backups: “nightly, to the cloud backup vault”; office entry: badge, visitors signed in and escorted.
steps.expectedOutput: D7 states what is logged and for how long, the first hour of an incident with the 72-hour notice, backup frequency and location, and visitor rules.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 — incident handling
docs.lookFor: the life-cycle figure; your seven steps map onto it

docs.title: NIST SP 800-92 — log management
docs.lookFor: what to log and how long to keep it; retention is a stated number

fixes.symptom: You do not know who should be notified first
fixes.fix: The Head of Security, then the CEO; the customer notice is a decision the CEO makes inside 72 hours.

fixes.symptom: Nightly backups do not exist yet
fixes.fix: Write the rule as the standard and keep S-5 open; week 4 builds and tests the backup.

steps.whatItMeans: The contract promises notice within 72 hours. An incident plan that names the hour-one steps is what keeps that promise under pressure.

tasks.title: Specify risk, assets and the metrics
tasks.objective: Put numbers on D1, D2 and D6: a scored risk register, a 25-asset inventory, six metrics, and eight control statements.
learn: Metrics with a formula and a target

docs.title: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 — risk assessment
docs.lookFor: Appendix G and H: the likelihood and impact scales you define five levels from

definitionOfDone: Ten scored risks including every planted weakness
One quantified risk
Inventory of 25 with custodian and end-of-support date
Six metrics with formula and target
Eight control statements

handoff.note: Contractors are screened before access — S-8.

steps.title: Score the risks and screen people (D1 v2)
steps.instruction: Define the scales, score ten risks, quantify one, and set screening by position.
instructionList: Scales: five likelihood levels (rare…almost certain), five impact levels (negligible…severe), a sentence each.
Risk row: “Shared admin login (S-2) · Identity · likelihood 4 · impact 5 · accounts + MFA · residual Low”.
Quantify one: “Ransomware on the old server: asset $40,000 × exposure 0.75 = SLE $30,000; ARO 0.5; ALE $15,000”.
Screening: “contractors screened before access and never given building codes” — S-8 closed.
steps.expectedOutput: D1 shows the two five-level scales, ten scored risks with treatment and residual, one quantified risk, and screening by position including contractors.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 — risk assessment
docs.lookFor: Appendix G and H: the likelihood and impact scales you define five levels from

docs.title: NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 — supply chain
docs.lookFor: supplier criticality tiers and the contract terms to flow down

fixes.symptom: Every risk scores 5 × 5
fixes.fix: Scales only work if they discriminate. Re-read the level definitions; most risks are 3 or 4 on one axis.

fixes.symptom: You have no asset value for the quantified risk
fixes.fix: Use the replacement cost from the scenario’s inventory; state the assumption beside the number.

steps.whatItMeans: A risk with no score cannot be ranked against another. The residual score is what the CEO accepts or sends back for more treatment.

steps.title: Grow the inventory to 25 (D2 v2)
steps.instruction: Reach 25 assets with custodian and end-of-support date, and the handling matrix.
instructionList: Row: “Old scheduling server · Operations · Confidential · on-premises · end of support 2023-10 (S-10)”.
Handling: a rule per level and data state (rest, transit, use); retention per record type; sanitization per storage.
Data migration inventory: what moves off the old server, where to, and the decommission plan.
steps.expectedOutput: D2 lists 25 assets with custodian, location and end-of-support date, the handling matrix by data state, and the migration inventory.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 — media sanitization
docs.lookFor: the clear / purge / destroy table by media type; the record you keep

docs.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 — Annex A themes
docs.lookFor: the four themes (organizational, people, physical, technological) your handling rules map to

fixes.symptom: End-of-support dates are hard to find
fixes.fix: Vendor lifecycle pages list them; for the old server’s OS it is already past — write the date, not “old”.

fixes.symptom: 25 feels padded
fixes.fix: Count keys, certificates, service accounts and backups as assets; they are the ones that get forgotten.

steps.whatItMeans: The handling matrix is where “encrypted” becomes a rule per level and state. S-10 is visible once the date is in the inventory.

steps.title: Metrics and control statements (D6, controls)
steps.description: Numbers to watch; controls to prove.
steps.where: Deliverables tab · D6 Assessment and Control Statements
steps.instruction: Write the Target Profile, six metrics, and the eight v2 control statements.
instructionList: D6 Profiles: target state per function; the gap per category becomes a remediation row.
Metric: “MFA coverage = admins with MFA ÷ all admins · source: identity provider · target 100%”; six like it.
Control statement: “IA-2 · D5 · a second factor on every administrative login; the IdP log is the record.”
Eight statements: PM-1, MP-6, SC-13, SC-7, IA-2, RA-5, IR-4, CM-3. Rescore: 16 of 32.
steps.expectedOutput: D6 shows the Target Profile, six metrics with formula, source and target, and a score of 16; the Control Statements form has eight filled rows.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — control catalogue
docs.lookFor: the control text for each id in your statements (PM-1, SC-7, IA-2…); copy its wording

docs.title: NIST SP 800-137 — continuous monitoring
docs.lookFor: metrics with a frequency and an owner

fixes.symptom: A control statement reads like the catalogue text
fixes.fix: The catalogue says what; your statement says who, how often, with what, and the record kept. Rewrite it.

fixes.symptom: A metric has no source
fixes.fix: Then nobody can compute it. Name the system that holds the number, or drop the metric.

steps.whatItMeans: A control statement is the sentence an assessor tests in week 5. Written as who-what-how often-record, it can be examined, not just admired.

tasks.title: Specify cryptography and the rule base
tasks.objective: Put numbers on D3, D4 and D8: a cryptography standard, a rule base, baselines and a secure-coding checklist.
learn: A security gate per development phase

docs.title: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 — key management
docs.lookFor: Table 2 key strengths and the crypto-period section: how long a key may live

definitionOfDone: D3 has a cryptography standard and six secure design principles on the diagram
D4 has a rule base and approved and banned protocols
D8 has a gate per phase and a ten-item coding checklist

handoff.note: Rescored in D6.

steps.title: Cryptography and design (D3 v2)
steps.instruction: Write the cryptography standard and place six design principles on the diagram.
instructionList: Standard: “TLS 1.3 only; AES-256-GCM at rest; ECDSA P-384 certificate; keys owned by Architecture; rotated yearly; destroyed on deletion”.
Three cryptanalytic attacks each matched to a control, e.g. “downgrade → TLS 1.3 only”.
Six principles on the diagram (least privilege, defence in depth, fail-safe…); model: Clark-Wilson, for transaction integrity.
steps.expectedOutput: D3 holds the cryptography standard with algorithms, key sizes, owner, rotation and destruction; three attack-to-control pairs; six principles placed; a justified model.

docs.title: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 — key management
docs.lookFor: Table 2 key strengths and the crypto-period section: how long a key may live

docs.title: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 — TLS
docs.lookFor: the required versions and cipher suites; TLS 1.3 is required, 1.2 the minimum

board.factOwn: Own fact: ticks, pastes and hashes by this member.
board.factTeam: Team fact: a document the team filled, approved or issued.
board.factContent: Content fact: read from the course and the registries.
board.notLoaded: Team facts load on the course page.
board.notLoadedOwn: Needs a fact not handed in: the cohort start date, the review queue or the page clock.
board.notMeasuredRole: Not measured in this course for this role.
board.importFailed: The file is not an environment profile
board.perTool: Verified steps on the tasks that use each tool
board.jsonCaption: The same thirty-two, the scores and the timing as the capstone-kpi-board/3 document an agent reads.
board.schemaNote: The shape is published as content/schemas/kpi-board.schema.json.
board.mapHowToRead: One star per competency this role practises, grouped by area; brighter means verified, a ring means the team approved the document.
board.mapIdle: Hover or focus a star to read it.
board.credentialClaim: An Open Badges 3.0 envelope around the member profile, unsigned: it carries no proof and claims none.
board.cohortLede: Counts per band for the members shown; nobody is ranked; team facts are judged through the review week.
board.packIdle: Hover or focus a socket to read it.
board.packKeys: Arrow keys move between sockets. Enter pins the read-out.
board.scoreNote: A weighted mean of the KPIs named; the weights are published in docs/SCORING.md.
board.timingNote: Minutes from the first paste to the verification, read from two recorded stamps; the median over steps resolved within a day.
board.noTiming: No step carries both stamps yet.
board.tierRule: Professional at ten verified uses across every course and retake; building below it, with the count.

DOMAINS.label: Technical capability
DOMAINS.definition: Skills, tools, commands and exam domains proven by pasted output that held every expected token.
DOMAINS.asks: Can this member operate the tools and run the commands the job needs?
DOMAINS.evidence: A verification record per step: the output hash, the tokens matched, the attempts, and a receipt in cloud mode.

DOMAINS.label: Professional execution
DOMAINS.definition: Procedures followed to standard, steps in order, first pastes, evidence named, checks met, documents controlled, work on time.
DOMAINS.asks: Does this member follow the runbook as written and deliver on the calendar?
DOMAINS.evidence: The order of verification stamps, the attempts, the file names, the Definition-of-Done checks, the control block and the cohort due dates.

DOMAINS.label: Problem solving
DOMAINS.definition: Faults logged and resolved, steps verified after a failed paste, stuck flags cleared, and the minutes from first paste to proof.
DOMAINS.asks: When something breaks, does this member find and fix it, and how long does it take?
DOMAINS.evidence: Fault, incident and triage rows with their outcome column, retries that verified, the append-only flag history and two stamps per step.

DOMAINS.label: Thought process
DOMAINS.definition: Decisions recorded against at least three options with rationale, rejected options, risk and rollback, and reasons written on change rows.
DOMAINS.asks: Does this member weigh options, say why, and plan the way back?
DOMAINS.evidence: Decision blocks with the option chosen, who chose it and when, the answers to the supporting questions, and the form lifecycle.

DOMAINS.label: Architecture and design
DOMAINS.definition: Design briefs, topologies, IP plans, bills of materials, decision records and as-built documents drafted, approved and issued.
DOMAINS.asks: Can this member design a system and write it down so another team can build it?
DOMAINS.evidence: The architecture and configuration forms of the role: rows filled, checks met, approved or issued, with the decisions on them.

DOMAINS.label: Team and communication
DOMAINS.definition: Hand-offs closed, RACI respected, peer reviews given, steps ticked for teammates, reports filed, notes written, handovers issued.
DOMAINS.asks: Does this member hand work on cleanly, review others and hold their lane?
DOMAINS.evidence: The lifecycle rows with who moved what, the hand-offs and their forms, the peer review queue, the reports and the notes.

DOMAINS.label: Learning and retention
DOMAINS.definition: Skills proved on a second task, verified again a week or more later, reused in another course, and the pace month on month.
DOMAINS.asks: Is this member still learning, and keeping what was learned?
DOMAINS.evidence: The verification stamps of every skill: first and last, the tasks and courses between them, and the last two months of them.

DOMAINS.label: Professional readiness
DOMAINS.definition: The tier per record item at ten verified uses, the exam weight verified, the work-role coverage and the readiness score.
DOMAINS.asks: Can this member consistently perform at a professional level in a real work environment?
DOMAINS.evidence: Every category of the record with its verified uses across courses, the published exam weights and the work roles’ required competencies.

KPIS.label: Skills verified
KPIS.numerator: Skills with at least one step verified from pasted output.
KPIS.denominator: Skills the role practises that carry a verifiable step.
KPIS.whyMember: Each verified skill names a task where the pasted output held every expected token.
KPIS.whyCompany: Skills backed by matched output rather than a tick, with the task behind each one named.

KPIS.label: Exam weight verified
KPIS.numerator: The published exam weight of every domain with a verified step, summed.
KPIS.denominator: The published exam weight of every domain the role practises, summed.
KPIS.whyMember: Shows which share of the exam blueprint the verified work already touches.
KPIS.whyCompany: Reads the verified work against the published exam domains and their weights.

KPIS.label: Commands verified
KPIS.numerator: Verified required steps that run a command.
KPIS.denominator: Verifiable required steps that run a command.
KPIS.whyMember: Command steps proven by their output; the table below splits them by tool.
KPIS.whyCompany: Tool use proven by output, per command step, split by tool in the table.

KPIS.label: Procedures to standard
KPIS.numerator: Followed procedures whose form cites a control code and was approved or issued.
KPIS.denominator: Procedures followed: every check due met and document control complete.
KPIS.whyMember: A runbook followed to a named control and approved by the team; a team fact.
KPIS.whyCompany: Procedures run to a cited NIST, ISO or SOC 2 control and approved by the team.

KPIS.label: Faults resolved
KPIS.numerator: Fault, incident and triage rows whose outcome column reads resolved.
KPIS.denominator: Fault, incident and triage rows the team filled on the forms of the role.
KPIS.whyMember: Every fault the team logged, and how many ended resolved; a team fact.
KPIS.whyCompany: Troubleshooting success read from the fault and incident records the team kept.

KPIS.label: Verified after retry
KPIS.numerator: Verified steps that took more than one paste.
KPIS.denominator: Verified steps.
KPIS.whyMember: A step that failed once and was then proven: the fault was found and fixed.
KPIS.whyCompany: How often a failed first paste was followed by a verified fix.

KPIS.label: Stuck flags cleared
KPIS.numerator: Stuck flags the member raised and later cleared.
KPIS.denominator: Stuck flags the member raised.
KPIS.whyMember: Asking for help and then getting past it both count; a flag never cleared says so.
KPIS.whyCompany: Blockers raised and worked through, from the append-only flag history.

KPIS.label: Time to resolution
KPIS.numerator: The median minutes from the first paste to the verification, per verified step with both stamps.
KPIS.denominator: Verified steps with both stamps; the share within the hour is the percentage.
KPIS.whyMember: The median, so one long gap moves nothing; a step left over a day is counted apart.
KPIS.whyCompany: Minutes from first attempt to proof, read from two recorded stamps, never a clock.

KPIS.label: Steps verified in order
KPIS.numerator: Tasks whose verifiable steps were verified in the authored order.
KPIS.denominator: Tasks with two or more verification records, so an order exists.
KPIS.whyMember: The procedure was run as written, step after step.
KPIS.whyCompany: Runbooks followed in order, read from the sequence of verification records.

KPIS.label: First-try verifications
KPIS.numerator: Verified steps whose first paste held every expected token.
KPIS.denominator: Verified steps.
KPIS.whyMember: Shown beside retries: a step verified after several pastes counts for as much.
KPIS.whyCompany: How often the first paste matched, printed beside how often it took more than one.

KPIS.label: Files named to convention
KPIS.numerator: Hashed files named to the evidence convention.
KPIS.denominator: Hashed files.
KPIS.whyMember: Evidence an auditor can find: date, team, tool and subject in every file name.
KPIS.whyCompany: Chain-of-custody hygiene: hashed files that follow the naming convention.

KPIS.label: Definition-of-Done met
KPIS.numerator: Definition-of-Done checks met on the forms of the role.
KPIS.denominator: Checks due on those forms through the current week.
KPIS.whyMember: Every check a form must pass this week, met or not, counted for the team.
KPIS.whyCompany: Work products measured against their own acceptance checks, week by week.

KPIS.label: Decisions recorded
KPIS.numerator: Decision blocks with an option chosen by this member.
KPIS.denominator: Decision blocks on the forms of the role, each with at least three options.
KPIS.whyMember: Each decision names the options weighed, the one chosen, who chose and when.
KPIS.whyCompany: Component, configuration and architecture choices made against named alternatives.

KPIS.label: Decisions justified
KPIS.numerator: Recorded decisions with every required supporting question answered.
KPIS.denominator: Decisions recorded by this member.
KPIS.whyMember: A choice with its reason, the rejected options and the risk accepted.
KPIS.whyCompany: Judgment shown in writing: rationale, rejected options, risk and rollback per decision.

KPIS.label: Decisions approved
KPIS.numerator: Recorded decisions on a form the team approved or issued.
KPIS.denominator: Decisions recorded by this member.
KPIS.whyMember: The team stood behind the choice; a team fact.
KPIS.whyCompany: Decisions that passed the team’s review and were issued.

KPIS.label: Changes with rollback
KPIS.numerator: Change-record rows with a rollback or back-out written.
KPIS.denominator: Change-record rows on the forms of the role.
KPIS.whyMember: Every change the team logged, and how many had a way back written down first.
KPIS.whyCompany: Change discipline: a rollback plan on every recorded change.

KPIS.label: Hand-offs completed
KPIS.numerator: Hand-offs whose named deliverable reached approved or issued.
KPIS.denominator: Hand-offs of the tasks of the role.
KPIS.whyMember: Work handed to another role that the team then approved or issued.
KPIS.whyCompany: Cross-role hand-offs closed by an approved document.

KPIS.label: RACI respected
KPIS.numerator: Lifecycle moves the member made in the role the RACI names for that move.
KPIS.denominator: Lifecycle moves the member made on forms with a RACI.
KPIS.whyMember: Submitting as the drafter, approving as the approver: the lane was held.
KPIS.whyCompany: Role discipline on documents, read from who moved what.

KPIS.label: Peer reviews given
KPIS.numerator: Blind peer reviews the member completed.
KPIS.denominator: Peer reviews assigned to the member.
KPIS.whyMember: Reviews of other teams’ frozen work, answered question by question.
KPIS.whyCompany: Review work done for others, from the blind review queue.

KPIS.label: Teammate steps ticked
KPIS.numerator: Required steps the member ticked on another role’s tasks.
KPIS.denominator: No denominator: a count.
KPIS.whyMember: Steps done on a teammate’s task, so a lane short of hands still finished.
KPIS.whyCompany: Help given across roles, counted in steps.

KPIS.label: On time
KPIS.numerator: Tasks whose last verification fell on or before the week due date.
KPIS.denominator: Tasks with a verification; needs the cohort start date.
KPIS.whyMember: The due date comes from the cohort calendar; without one the row says so.
KPIS.whyCompany: Reliability against a calendar, read from the verification stamps and the cohort start.

KPIS.label: Document control complete
KPIS.numerator: Forms with data whose document-control block is complete.
KPIS.denominator: Forms of the role with data.
KPIS.whyMember: Id, version, owner, date and status on every document the team filled.
KPIS.whyCompany: Document control kept on every filled form: id, version, owner, date, status.

KPIS.label: Controls cited
KPIS.numerator: Distinct control codes on approved or issued forms the role drafts.
KPIS.denominator: Distinct control codes the forms of the role cite.
KPIS.whyMember: The published controls the approved documents cite, by code.
KPIS.whyCompany: Control codes practised through approved documents, by standard.

KPIS.label: Instructor approved
KPIS.numerator: Forms of the role whose latest instructor review is approved.
KPIS.denominator: Forms of the role.
KPIS.whyMember: Forms an instructor reviewed and approved; the latest review per form counts.
KPIS.whyCompany: Forms with an instructor verdict of approved, the latest review per form.

KPIS.label: Skills proved twice
KPIS.numerator: Skills with verified steps on two or more distinct tasks.
KPIS.denominator: Skills with at least one verified step.
KPIS.whyMember: A skill verified on two different tasks was carried from one context to another.
KPIS.whyCompany: Verification repeated on a second task is harder to reach by luck or by copying.

KPIS.label: Skills retained
KPIS.numerator: Skills verified again seven or more days after their first verification.
KPIS.denominator: Skills with at least one verified step.
KPIS.whyMember: Proof a week or more apart: the skill stayed.
KPIS.whyCompany: Retention read from the gap between two verification stamps on the same skill.

KPIS.label: Learning velocity
KPIS.numerator: Verified steps in the twenty-eight days before the page clock.
KPIS.denominator: Verified steps in the twenty-eight days before those; the percentage caps at one hundred.
KPIS.whyMember: This month against last: rising, level or slowing, from the verification stamps.
KPIS.whyCompany: Pace of verified work, month on month, from recorded stamps.

KPIS.label: Profile coverage
KPIS.numerator: Required competencies of the selected work role or environment profile at verified or better.
KPIS.denominator: Required competencies the selected work role or environment profile names.
KPIS.whyMember: Measures the verified skills against a job role or a published company profile, with the untaught gap named.
KPIS.whyCompany: Coverage of the competencies a work role or an environment profile requires, read from verified steps.

KPIS.label: Values recalled
KPIS.numerator: Recall activities answered correctly: the value the team recorded, picked among distractors.
KPIS.denominator: Recall activities answered, from the checkpoints reached.
KPIS.whyMember: Weeks after recording an address, a prefix, a port or a decision, the member still knows it.
KPIS.whyCompany: Retention of the project the member built, read from answers given without the form open.

KPIS.label: Scenarios applied
KPIS.numerator: Applied scenarios answered correctly: an address inside the prefix, a free port on the host, the committed size.
KPIS.denominator: Applied scenarios offered at the checkpoints reached.
KPIS.whyMember: Takes a value the team recorded and uses it under a change the course did not script.
KPIS.whyCompany: Applied use of recorded facts, not recall alone; offered scenarios count whether or not answered.

KPIS.label: Conflicts resolved
KPIS.numerator: Conflicts the record found that the team resolved: the address, the port, the prefix, the size no longer at odds.
KPIS.denominator: Conflicts the record found at the checkpoints reached, resolved or still open.
KPIS.whyMember: A duplicate address or an over-committed host found by the platform and fixed by the team.
KPIS.whyCompany: Contradictions in the record closed, read from the record itself rather than from a claim.

KPIS.label: Minutes on task
KPIS.numerator: Whole minutes the member had tasks of this course open on a visible tab, pauses excluded.
KPIS.denominator: A count; nothing is read into it.
KPIS.whyMember: How long the work took the member, by the timer they can pause; measured, never rewarded.
KPIS.whyCompany: Time on task as context for the other rows; no score reads it.

KPI_FAMILIES.label: Technical capability

KPI_FAMILIES.asks: Can this member operate the tools and run the procedures the job needs?

KPI_FAMILIES.label: Problem solving
KPI_FAMILIES.definition: Faults logged and resolved, verifications reached after a failed paste, stuck flags cleared, and the minutes between first paste and proof.
KPI_FAMILIES.asks: When something breaks, does this member find and fix it, and how long does it take?

KPI_FAMILIES.label: Professional execution
KPI_FAMILIES.definition: How the work was done: steps in order, first pastes, evidence named to convention, every check due met.
KPI_FAMILIES.asks: Does this member follow the runbook as written and leave evidence an auditor can find?

KPI_FAMILIES.label: Decision making
KPI_FAMILIES.definition: Decisions recorded against at least three options, justified, approved by the team, and changes with a rollback written.
KPI_FAMILIES.asks: Does this member weigh options, say why, and plan the way back?

KPI_FAMILIES.label: Teamwork
KPI_FAMILIES.definition: Hand-offs closed, RACI respected, peer reviews given and steps ticked on teammates’ tasks.
KPI_FAMILIES.asks: Does this member hand work on cleanly and hold their lane in a team?

KPI_FAMILIES.label: Professionalism
KPI_FAMILIES.definition: On time against the cohort calendar, documents controlled, controls cited, instructor approval earned.
KPI_FAMILIES.asks: Does this member deliver on time, to standard, and to the reviewer’s satisfaction?

KPI_FAMILIES.label: Growth
KPI_FAMILIES.definition: Skills proved twice, retained across weeks, verified faster week on week, and the gap to a work role closing.
KPI_FAMILIES.asks: Is this member still learning, and keeping what was learned?

KPI_FAMILIES.label: Understanding
KPI_FAMILIES.definition: Values the team recorded, recalled and applied weeks later; conflicts the record found, resolved; minutes on task, measured.
KPI_FAMILIES.asks: Did this member retain what the team built, and can they apply it when something changes?

METRICS.definition: Skills verified again on a later task seven or more days after the first, over skills verified.
METRICS.note: R132: read from the stamps of verification records.

METRICS.label: Calibration
METRICS.definition: Stated confidence that matched the outcome, over stated confidences.

METRICS.label: Fixes consulted
METRICS.definition: "If it does not work" rows opened before a verification, over verifications.

METRICS.label: Documentation opened
METRICS.definition: Documentation links opened per task.

METRICS.label: On time
METRICS.definition: Tasks whose last verification fell on or before the week due date, over tasks verified; needs the cohort start date.
METRICS.note: R132: two recorded stamps, the verification and the due date. R136: loads wherever the cohort has a start date.

METRICS.label: Time on task
METRICS.definition: Minutes from the first paste to the last verification of a task.
METRICS.note: R132: a step has no start stamp; the first paste is the earliest fact.

METRICS.label: Time to resolution
METRICS.definition: Median minutes from the first paste to the verification per verified step with both stamps; over 24 hours counted apart.
METRICS.note: R132: two recorded stamps; the median, so one long gap moves nothing.

METRICS.label: Time against estimate
METRICS.definition: Minutes from first paste to verification against the authored estimate of the task.
METRICS.note: R132: computable from the same stamps; not wired this round.

METRICS.label: Ranking
METRICS.definition: Any ordering of members against each other.
METRICS.note: Nothing is ranked.

METRICS.label: Faults logged
METRICS.definition: Fault, incident and triage rows the team filled on the forms of the role, over such rows the course expects.
METRICS.note: A team fact; loads on the course page.

METRICS.label: Faults resolved
METRICS.definition: Fault, incident and triage rows whose outcome column reads resolved, over rows filled.
METRICS.note: A team fact; loads on the course page.

METRICS.label: Stuck flags cleared
METRICS.definition: Stuck flags the member raised and later cleared, over flags raised.
METRICS.note: R132: the flag history is append-only. R136: loads on every surface.

METRICS.label: Decisions offered
METRICS.definition: Decision blocks on the forms of the role, each with at least three options.

METRICS.label: Decisions recorded
METRICS.definition: Decision blocks with an option chosen by this member, over decision blocks on the forms of the role.
METRICS.note: The choice carries who made it and when. Loads on the course page.

METRICS.label: Decisions justified
METRICS.definition: Recorded decisions with every required supporting question answered, over decisions recorded.
METRICS.note: Loads on the course page.

METRICS.label: Decisions approved
METRICS.definition: Recorded decisions on a form the team approved or issued, over decisions recorded.
METRICS.note: Loads on the course page.

METRICS.label: Reasons written
METRICS.definition: Free-text rationale fields filled on the forms of the role, over such fields.
METRICS.note: Team rows carry no author. Loads on the course page.

METRICS.label: Review marks met
METRICS.definition: Instructor marks per rubric category that passed, over marks given on the forms of the role.
METRICS.note: R132: one mark per category per verdict, kept as history. Loads on the course page.

METRICS.label: Execution rows
METRICS.definition: In order, first try, evidence named, checks met, control complete and on time, as rows of the Professional Execution domain.

METRICS.label: Skills reused across courses
METRICS.definition: Skills verified in two or more courses, over skills verified anywhere.
METRICS.note: A portfolio fact: read across the member’s courses.

METRICS.label: Professional tier
METRICS.definition: Record items with ten or more verified uses across every course and retake, over items with any verified use.
METRICS.note: R132: the threshold is ten; below it the item reads as building, with the count.

METRICS.label: Cohort domain coverage
METRICS.definition: Per cohort, members with at least one verified step per domain, over members. Instructor aggregate.

METRICS.label: Funnel stages
METRICS.definition: Members who reached each stage in turn, from enrolled to capstone filed, over members enrolled. Instructor aggregate.
METRICS.note: Counts per cohort; nobody named.

METRICS.label: Active weeks bands
METRICS.definition: Members per band of graded weeks with any tick: none, one, two or three, four or more. Instructor aggregate.

METRICS.label: Step friction
METRICS.definition: Per verifiable step, members ticked without verification, stuck, or stopped before it, over members with the task.
METRICS.note: Steps are ordered, never people.

METRICS.label: Course verifiability
METRICS.definition: Verifiable required steps over required steps per course. Content only.

METRICS.label: Course skill coverage
METRICS.definition: Skills, tools, procedures, standards, tactics and practices per course. Content only.

METRICS.label: Cross-platform signal
METRICS.definition: A competency-level statement shared with another platform.

METRICS.label: Profile coverage
METRICS.definition: Required competencies of a work role or an environment profile at verified or better, over required; the untaught remainder is named.

METRICS.label: Skills proved twice
METRICS.definition: Skills with verified steps on two or more distinct tasks, over skills with a verified step.

METRICS.label: Skills current
METRICS.definition: Skills whose last verification falls inside the currency window, over skills verified.
METRICS.note: A window of days the page supplies; never a duration shown.

METRICS.label: Capstone filed
METRICS.definition: The course capstone document issued by the team, one per course, with the weeks cleared beside it.
METRICS.note: A team fact; loads on the course page.

METRICS.label: Ability estimate
METRICS.definition: A latent ability per objective estimated from item responses on a practice platform.
METRICS.note: The practice platform’s side; only a competency-level conclusion may cross, with consent.

METRICS.label: Readiness band
METRICS.definition: A pass-likelihood band per exam, validated against reported outcomes.
METRICS.note: The practice platform’s side; needs reported outcomes and consent.

METRICS.label: Transfer to unseen scenarios
METRICS.definition: Verified work on a scenario never practised before, over such scenarios.
METRICS.note: Needs scenario provenance per event.

METRICS.label: Unassisted verifications
METRICS.definition: Steps verified with no hint, tutor or agent assistance, over verified steps.
METRICS.note: Needs the assist level recorded per event.

METRICS.label: Rubric verdicts as events
METRICS.definition: The four category verdicts of each frozen submission, appended as events.
METRICS.note: The verdicts exist as rows today.

METRICS.label: Placement reported
METRICS.definition: Members who reported a role after a course, over members who answered with the outcome grant on.
METRICS.note: Counts only, shown from five answers; the employer name stays with the member.

METRICS.label: Used at work
METRICS.definition: Members who reported using a course at work, over members who answered with the outcome grant on.
METRICS.note: Self-reported by the member; an employer report needs a data agreement.

METRICS.label: Platform return
METRICS.definition: Cost per verified competency, and employer ramp saved, as the parties report them.
METRICS.note: Needs cost and employer data nobody has handed in.

METRICS.label: Time to competency
METRICS.definition: Days from the first verification of a skill to its tenth verified use.
METRICS.note: R132: the professional threshold is ten verified uses across courses.

METRICS.label: Task time against benchmark
METRICS.definition: Minutes to resolve a task against a published service-level baseline.
METRICS.note: R132: no baseline is published yet.

METRICS.label: Learning velocity
METRICS.definition: Verified steps in the twenty-eight days before the page clock, over verified steps in the twenty-eight days before those.
METRICS.note: R132: the page passes the clock; the projection reads none.

METRICS.label: Values recalled
METRICS.definition: Recall activities answered correctly, over recall activities answered, at the checkpoints reached.
METRICS.note: R140: the activity asks for a value the team recorded; the distractors come from the record.

METRICS.label: Scenarios applied
METRICS.definition: Applied scenarios answered correctly, over applied scenarios offered at the checkpoints reached.
METRICS.note: R140: an address inside the prefix, a free port on the host, the committed size doubled.

METRICS.label: Conflicts resolved
METRICS.definition: Conflicts the record found that are no longer present, over conflicts found, once the apply checkpoint is reached.
METRICS.note: R140: read from the record itself; the answer only says the team looked.

METRICS.label: Minutes on task
METRICS.definition: Whole minutes the member had tasks open on a visible tab, pauses and hidden tabs excluded; a count.
METRICS.note: R140: the timer the member can pause; measured, never rewarded.

PRACTICES.label: Least privilege
PRACTICES.definition: Every account, role and agent holds only the rights its task needs, and nothing it might need later.

PRACTICES.label: Defence in depth
PRACTICES.definition: More than one control stands between an attacker and the asset, so one failure is not a breach.

PRACTICES.label: Default deny
PRACTICES.definition: Nothing passes a boundary unless a rule allows it; the allow list is the policy.

PRACTICES.label: Network segmentation
PRACTICES.definition: Zones with distinct trust levels are separated, and the flows between them are named and limited.

PRACTICES.label: Zero trust access
PRACTICES.definition: No request is trusted for where it comes from; identity, device and context decide every access.

PRACTICES.label: Multi-factor authentication
PRACTICES.definition: Every console and privileged login asks for a second factor; a password alone is refused.

PRACTICES.label: Federated identity
PRACTICES.definition: Applications trust one identity provider over SAML or OIDC instead of keeping their own passwords.

PRACTICES.label: Machine identity register
PRACTICES.definition: Every service account, key and certificate has an owner and a rotation date in one register.

PRACTICES.label: Separation of duties
PRACTICES.definition: The person who requests, the person who approves and the person who applies a change are not the same.

PRACTICES.label: Periodic access review
PRACTICES.definition: Accounts and rights are reviewed on a schedule; orphans are disabled and the review is recorded.

PRACTICES.label: Joiner and leaver process
PRACTICES.definition: Access is granted on a documented request and removed within a stated time of leaving.

PRACTICES.label: Encryption in transit
PRACTICES.definition: Traffic crosses a boundary only over approved TLS versions, and the weak ones are refused.

PRACTICES.label: Key rotation
PRACTICES.definition: Keys and certificates have an owner and a rotation date, and a rotation is recorded when it happens.

PRACTICES.label: Retest to closure
PRACTICES.definition: A finding is closed only by a retest that shows the fix, and every finding ends Closed, Open or Risk accepted.

PRACTICES.label: Likelihood-times-impact scoring
PRACTICES.definition: Each risk is scored on a stated scale for likelihood and impact, and the score decides the order.

PRACTICES.label: Threat modelling
PRACTICES.definition: Threats are enumerated per component with a method, and each is tied to a control or an accepted risk.

PRACTICES.label: Tabletop exercise
PRACTICES.definition: The team walks through an incident on paper with injects, and the after-action report names improvements.

PRACTICES.label: Change control
PRACTICES.definition: Every change is requested, reviewed, reversible and recorded before it reaches a system.

PRACTICES.label: Configuration scanning
PRACTICES.definition: Hosts are scanned against a benchmark on a schedule, and the failed checks become findings.

PRACTICES.label: Media sanitisation
PRACTICES.definition: Storage is cleared, purged or destroyed to the written level before it leaves, and the action is recorded.

PRACTICES.label: Pipeline gates
PRACTICES.definition: A build cannot proceed past a scan, a test or an approval that failed; a gate that blocks is a control.

PRACTICES.label: Dependency and image scanning
PRACTICES.definition: Third-party packages and container images are scanned for known vulnerabilities before release.

PRACTICES.label: Software bill of materials
PRACTICES.definition: A release lists its components (CycloneDX or SPDX), so a vulnerable dependency can be found.

PRACTICES.label: Backups tested by restore
PRACTICES.definition: A backup counts only after a restore from it has been performed and its hashes compared.

PRACTICES.label: Recovery objectives
PRACTICES.definition: Recovery time and recovery point targets are written per service, and a drill is timed against them.

PRACTICES.label: Centralised logging
PRACTICES.definition: Every host ships its logs to one place where they are kept, searched and alerted on.

PRACTICES.label: Written policy
PRACTICES.definition: Rules are written as shall statements with an owner, a review date and the standard they implement.

PRACTICES.label: Written runbooks
PRACTICES.definition: Routine operations are written as steps a colleague could follow, and the steps are kept current.

PRACTICES.label: Sign and version documents
PRACTICES.definition: A document carries an id, a version, an owner, a date and a status, and a change makes a new version.

PRACTICES.label: Asset inventory
PRACTICES.definition: Every asset is listed with an owner, a location and a classification before it is protected.

PRACTICES.label: Data classification
PRACTICES.definition: Information is classified on a written scale, and handling rules follow the class.

PRACTICES.label: Personal data discovery
PRACTICES.definition: Stores are scanned for personal data before and after a clean-up, and the counts are recorded.

PRACTICES.label: Control mapping
PRACTICES.definition: Each control is mapped to the criteria it satisfies across frameworks, with an owner and an evidence source.

PRACTICES.label: Evidence by design
PRACTICES.definition: Every control names the evidence that proves it operates, and the evidence is collected as the work happens.

PRACTICES.label: Corrective action
PRACTICES.definition: Every nonconformity gets a cause, a corrective action, an owner and a date, and the action is checked.

PRACTICES.label: Supplier tiering
PRACTICES.definition: Suppliers are tiered by the access and data they hold, and the top tier carries written terms.

PRACTICES.label: Write for leadership
PRACTICES.definition: A report opens with what a non-technical reader must decide, and the technical detail follows.

PRACTICES.label: Metrics with targets
PRACTICES.definition: Each metric has a formula, a source and a target, so a number can be read as good or bad.

SCORING.label: Tool proficiency
SCORING.definition: Commands and skills proven by output, and skills proved on a second task, weighted.
SCORING.caveat: Reads browser checks and receipts of stamps, not proof of the machine; the per-tool table names each command.

SCORING.label: Troubleshooting success
SCORING.definition: Faults resolved, retries that verified, stuck flags cleared and steps resolved within the hour, weighted.
SCORING.caveat: Faults are team rows; the minutes are a median between two recorded stamps, so a step left open overnight is counted apart.

SCORING.label: Judgment
SCORING.definition: Decisions recorded, justified and approved, and changes with a rollback written, equally weighted.
SCORING.caveat: Counts what was written against named options; it does not judge whether the choice was right.

SCORING.label: Collaboration
SCORING.definition: Hand-offs closed, RACI respected and peer reviews given, weighted.
SCORING.caveat: Team facts count for the team; the role share on the KPIs says what this member moved.

SCORING.label: Reliability
SCORING.definition: On time against the cohort calendar, document control complete, controls cited and instructor approval, weighted.
SCORING.caveat: On time needs the cohort start date; without one the score stands on the other three and says so.

SCORING.label: Readiness
SCORING.definition: Exam weight verified, work-role coverage, skills retained and steps in order, weighted.
SCORING.caveat: A reading of the record against an exam and a work role, not a prediction of a pass or a hire.

SCORING.label: Understanding retained
SCORING.definition: Values recalled, scenarios applied and conflicts resolved, weeks after the team recorded them, weighted.
SCORING.caveat: Asks only about values the team recorded; before the checkpoint week the score stands on nothing and says so.

SOPS.label: Incident response plan
SOPS.definition: The written plan for handling an incident: roles, the first hour, containment, communication and the notice deadline.

SOPS.label: Change record
SOPS.definition: A change written before it is made: what, where, the backup, the approval, the rollback and the result.

SOPS.label: Release record
SOPS.definition: What a release contains, what blocked, what was tested and who approved it going out.

SOPS.label: Recovery drill
SOPS.definition: A timed restore or failover against the written targets, with the hashes compared and the gap recorded.

SOPS.label: Backup plan
SOPS.definition: What is backed up, how often, where it goes, how long it is kept and how a restore is tested.

SOPS.label: Risk register
SOPS.definition: Each risk with its likelihood, impact, score, owner and treatment, reviewed on a schedule.

SOPS.label: Supplier review
SOPS.definition: Suppliers tiered by access and data, with terms for the top tier and a review date.

SOPS.label: Security policy
SOPS.definition: Shall statements with an owner, a review date and the standard each one implements.

SOPS.label: Data handling standard

SOPS.label: Access review
SOPS.definition: Accounts and rights checked against the access matrix, orphans disabled, the review recorded.

SOPS.label: Identity and access standard
SOPS.definition: Roles against systems, the MFA rule, joiner and leaver timing, separation of duties.

SOPS.label: Asset inventory

SOPS.label: Control mapping

SOPS.label: Customer assurance response
